# Invariants (N-PK)

<!-- generated by scripts/verify_docs.py --write-nav; do not hand-edit -->

> Code is the source of truth. This file is a map; when it and the code disagree, the code wins.

Every invariant is defined in exactly one file and referenced by id elsewhere.

The index is sharded by family letter: see also [`doctrine/invariants.md`](invariants.md), [`doctrine/invariants-c-d.md`](invariants-c-d.md), [`doctrine/invariants-e.md`](invariants-e.md), [`doctrine/invariants-f-m.md`](invariants-f-m.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pl-pq.md`](invariants-pl-pq.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pr-r.md`](invariants-pr-r.md), [`doctrine/invariants-s.md`](invariants-s.md), [`doctrine/invariants-t-z.md`](invariants-t-z.md).

| Id | Statement | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| `INV-OBS-001` | A correlation id arriving on the request header is validated to a fixed shape; one supplied inside an invocation payload is not. | [`architecture/observability.md`](../architecture/observability.md) |
| `INV-OBS-003` | The health endpoint returns a fixed success response without consulting any subsystem. | [`architecture/observability.md`](../architecture/observability.md) |
| `INV-OBS-004` | Redaction runs at every point the application's own logging pipeline turns record content into text — the filter for message and arguments, the formatters for exception text, stack text and structured extras. | [`architecture/observability.md`](../architecture/observability.md) |
| `INV-OBS-005` | Every in_casa engagement turn logs under a cid minted as the turn opens — the session reader's lines for that turn's frames, and its SDK read-task (tool-callback) lines while it is the session's running turn — and, as it opens, one INFO line under that cid ties it to the engagement id and the engaging cid. | [`architecture/observability.md`](../architecture/observability.md) |
| `INV-OPS-001` | When the install or upgrade pending-configuration merge cannot read or validate `InstanceDir.desired()`, its refusal instructs preservation of the pending candidate, its saved configuration, and the receipt and staging tree needed to resume, followed by resolving the failure and retrying. These two refusal paths do not recommend uninstalling or starting afresh. | [`doctrine/operating-casa.md`](../doctrine/operating-casa.md) |
| `INV-OUT-001` | Model-authored text reaches the Telegram transport only as an `Admitted` minted by the authoring turn's scope — `send`, `send_response`, `finalize_stream`, `finalize_response_stream`, `post_dm_keyboard` and `send_media`'s caption refuse a bare string with an error log, zero Bot API calls and the method's own failure value. | [`architecture/output-boundary.md`](../architecture/output-boundary.md) |
| `INV-OUT-002` | In a turn where inbound files were listed and none read or handed off, every model-text emission committed after the listing carries the disclosure line at its head — streamed cumulatives included — and when a streamed reply's page-1 unit did not land, the line goes out once as its own message before the overflow pages; after a successful `Read` or hand-off of any armed file none does; a turn that received a file of its own owes that file alone; a turn with no file of its own is never told the person sent it files; and a silent turn stays silent. | [`architecture/output-boundary.md`](../architecture/output-boundary.md) |
| `INV-OUT-003` | A payload stored under an undischarged obligation — a reminder's text, a delegation or engagement brief — is delivered with its resolved note by the turn that sends it, whatever that turn's model writes; a payload stored after the `Read` carries none; and an inherited note is never discharged. | [`architecture/output-boundary.md`](../architecture/output-boundary.md) |
| `INV-OUT-004` | A delegated child runs under the view its launcher built at entry — the launcher's identity and markers plus the launch-time note, never the pooled holder's current contents — and an emitting handler that outlives its turn commits under the scope it captured at entry. | [`architecture/output-boundary.md`](../architecture/output-boundary.md) |
| `INV-OUT-005` | A tool that emits or stores annotated text reports the exact line in its result. | [`architecture/output-boundary.md`](../architecture/output-boundary.md) |
| `INV-OUT-006` | Whether a turn streams, whether its final reply is closing silence, and where an untrusted webhook turn's discrete send goes are properties of its scope — the first and third registered at mint from the message's own facts, the second intrinsic to final-reply admission: a scheduled turn or an event wake never receives a token callback, a final reply that strips to nothing but `<silent/>` sentinels is suppressed by admission while prose after a sentinel is delivered whole — on a streaming turn, the final reply and every stream update without a leading or closing run of `<silent/>` sentinels, a sentinel anywhere else kept — except that when a scheduled turn's or an event wake's last text-bearing message strips to a `<silent/>` after earlier text, the reply is suppressed if the turn made at least one Casa send, every one confirmed delivered, every send call resolved without failure, and exactly one attempt ran with no retry, and is otherwise the earlier messages without the closing ones — and an untrusted webhook turn's `send_message` is bound to Telegram whatever channel it named, while its final reply is delivered only when its route declares `deliver: operator` or `operator_always`, and then on every output path only to the operator's Telegram with a fresh delivery context; and when the winning attempt folded the result of a call the authorization hook left waiting on the operator's approval — or of a synchronous `delegate_to_agent` call whose child's run left one waiting — with no later result of a call that consumed the same grant, directly or in such a delegate's child, the final reply is only the text-bearing messages folded before that result, and is suppressed, not chosen, when they strip to silence. | [`architecture/output-scope-properties.md`](../architecture/output-scope-properties.md) |
| `INV-OWN-001` | A surface of an agent — a plugin call that delivers a slot or asks Casa, `send_media`, `ask_operator`, a job start — posts only at its task's delivery, in that agent's own open chat (the resident's chat being its own); with no open own chat, or a task born without a delivery, the call is refused with a typed line before the plugin runs, and nothing is ever posted in another chat instead. | [`architecture/own-voice.md`](../architecture/own-voice.md) |
| `INV-OWN-002` | A task's delivery is decided once, by its launcher, at its birth — the resident's chat for the resident, the executor's own chat when it is open at that moment, otherwise none — and is carried unchanged by its origin, its records and its binding for the task's whole life; a task born without one posts nothing even after the chat opens. | [`architecture/own-voice.md`](../architecture/own-voice.md) |
| `INV-OWN-003` | A task's result goes to its requester, the agent whose turn started it; an agent's conversation receives the results of work it started and only a body-free note of work another agent started, and a task in an agent's open chat posts there the message it closed its turn with (nothing when that is silence) while the requester gets its bounded result. | [`architecture/own-voice.md`](../architecture/own-voice.md) |
| `INV-OWN-004` | Every landed post of a task is filed under that task, keyed by bot, chat and message, found again after a reload; an operator's reply or file quoting a live task's post goes into that task — queued in order while it is pending, never to a conversation — and a reply to an ended task's post, or any other message, is the chat's own agent's turn. | [`architecture/own-voice.md`](../architecture/own-voice.md) |
| `INV-OWN-005` | A file sent to a live task is stored in the executor's own inbox and readable by that task alone — the grant is one exact path, asked at each Read, so a file granted while the task runs is readable at once — and a file whose task ended meanwhile stays in the inbox and the operator is told. | [`architecture/own-voice.md`](../architecture/own-voice.md) |
| `INV-OWN-006` | An update that reaches an agent's own bot passes the lifecycle's intake before it is queued; it is delivered only to a bound, reconciled, declared agent whose queue is registered and with nothing older held, otherwise journaled before Telegram is acknowledged, and held records are released in arrival order, a refused one holding itself and every later one. | [`architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-OWN-008` | Every lifecycle effect finds its phase on disk, every phase has a boot reconciliation, and a bot is released only on the token fetch failure that establishes its deletion; every other failure keeps it recovering. | [`architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-OWN-009` | A tap on the resident's bot on a card whose agent now declares its own chat is answered with one line naming that chat and runs, edits, claims and reserves nothing; a Casa card, the resident's own card and any tap on an agent's own bot are untouched. | [`architecture/own-voice.md`](../architecture/own-voice.md) |
| `INV-OWN-010` | An agent that declares its own chat keeps one conversation, on the bus under its role, built with the specialist's surface and session extras — never the resident's builder — fed by the operator's direct messages in its chat; `/new` there ends only that conversation's session and its pad. | [`architecture/own-voice.md`](../architecture/own-voice.md) |
| `INV-OWN-011` | The operator's first turn in an agent's own chat that the agent's queue accepts, whatever it says, opens the chat: that turn alone carries Casa's line that the operator just opened it — in an agent's new chat after a move to a new bot, the line that it is the new chat — and `chat_open_at` is persisted only after the acceptance, on a first send and on a retry after a hand-back alike; a delivery refused or interrupted, across a restart included, and a file sent without a caption open nothing, and the chat's next accepted operator turn carries the line. | [`architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-OWN-012` | A bot is registered only from the operator's own `managed_bot_created` message to Casa's bot in his chat, and bound to an agent only when its username equals that agent's current suggestion (a waiting agent's first bot, or a pending change) or the operator names a waiting agent; a bot is never rebound to another agent, and an agent has one bound bot at a time. | [`architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-OWN-013` | A pending switch is applied only by the boot step that runs before Casa's HTTP server, channels, workers and scheduler start, and only when no durable record still waits on the old bot; it removes the old bot's record, held journal and stored token before the new bot enters binding, and a stored token is used only for the bot whose id it begins with. | [`architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-OWN-014` | An offer's handle is refused when it is not a valid bot username, when it was ever offered to another agent, or when the t.me probe shows it taken; a probe that cannot complete refuses nothing. | [`architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/own-voice-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-PAD-001` | The `scratchpad` tool takes no argument that selects a pad and refuses any it does not declare; each client's tool works only on the key it was built with, which for a delegated client is its run's session, so two sessions have two pads and a relay turn cannot read its worker's. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-002` | Every `scratchpad` reply stays under 50,000 characters, the size past which the CLI's documentation says a reply goes to a file, whatever the pad holds or the call repeats, and while the pad exists opens with its shape, naming at most 20 sections; a read gives at most 100 lines or 8,000 characters unless asked for more and at most 40,000 characters, cuts a long line at 2,000 with the offset that reads on, says what comes next, and a search gives at most 40 lines cut at 300 with its true total. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-003` | `BindingStore.adopt` moves the session's pad to the session it adopts, leaving a copy only when another binding still names the old session. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-004` | A delegated run's pad goes when the run returns, raises or is cancelled unless a kept binding names its session; a binding's pad goes when the last binding naming the session is dropped; a pad unused for 24 hours goes unless a kept binding names its session or it is a job's; and a request's stop or end deletes no pad. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-005` | A stored call's client, and one whose role disallows the tool, has no pad tool, no grant and no line about the pad in its system prompt; every other delegated client has all three. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-006` | A `scratchpad` write or append that would make a second section of one name, and an operation that names a section two sections share, changes nothing and says why, on the tool and on the pad route alike. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-007` | A delegated run that is not a continuation opens its pad, when none exists under its key, with one `## brief` section holding its task and, when the turn has them, the operator's own words; a continuation writes no brief, and a pad that exists is never seeded. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-008` | `POST /internal/broker/pad` reaches only the pad whose tool was built for the broker client id the request presents, which `attach` registers from the client's env, and answers only while that client has exactly one call in flight; no field of the request selects a pad, an id registered for two pads reaches neither, and a read gives at most 30,000 characters of one section with the offset that reads on. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-009` | Text the pad route writes or appends keeps its lines, but a line beginning `## ` is stored with one leading space, so a plugin's text never starts a section. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-010` | A background job's pad is keyed by its engagement id and opened by every job session build, seeded with a brief only by a launch and only when neither memory nor its file holds one; every change is written atomically, as a JSON list of its lines, to `/data/job-pads/<id>.pad` (0600); a build with no pad in memory loads that file; idle expiry never drops it; and it is deleted, file included, on every path that ends the job and at boot for an id that is unknown or durably ended. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-011` | After a compaction, a job session's `SessionStart` text carries, after the job header, its pad's page-text sentence, its shape and its `## brief` section cut at 4,000 characters, when the pad holds anything. | [`architecture/scratchpad.md`](../architecture/scratchpad.md) |
| `INV-PAD-012` | A `run` changes its own pad only on exit 0, all at once, only when the pad's stamp is the snapshot's, never past the cap, round-trips an unchanged pad byte for byte (header spelling, blank lines and lone surrogates included), and its reply stays inside INV-PAD-002. | [`architecture/script-runner.md`](../architecture/script-runner.md) |
| `INV-PAD-013` | The box runs no script unless its label is Casa's with `//pyrun (enforce)`, the sentinel named by the child profile text's digest opens, a socket, a world-readable file, a user namespace, an exec, a SysV segment and a session key are refused, no descriptor above 2 is open, its parent is Casa, and its identity is the slot's uid with empty capabilities; and a run with no ready frame is the box's failure whatever its status. | [`architecture/script-runner.md`](../architecture/script-runner.md) |
| `INV-PAD-014` | Every run ends with a kill of its slot's uid, and a slot is reused only after a kill the ladder verified. | [`architecture/script-runner.md`](../architecture/script-runner.md) |
| `INV-PASS-004` | A delegation result or notice whose delegate closed its turn with a message that is only silence ends with Casa's note that the delegate has nothing for the person; a closing message with words, or an empty one, carries no such note. | [`architecture/delegate-closing-message.md`](../architecture/delegate-closing-message.md) |
| `INV-PERS-001` | When a resident has an activated compiled bundle, that bundle's projection is the base prompt; the composed prompt is a fallback for when there is none. | [`architecture/personality.md`](../architecture/personality.md) |
| `INV-PERS-002` | Persona validation is structural; it does not verify that a persona's claims about capability are true. | [`architecture/personality.md`](../architecture/personality.md) |
| `INV-PERS-003` | A resident's binding reconciliation runs as part of loading and is not isolated from it. | [`architecture/personality.md`](../architecture/personality.md) |
| `INV-PERS-004` | The restricted-origin prompt omits the persona section. | [`architecture/personality.md`](../architecture/personality.md) |
| `INV-PERS-005` | The persona packs the image ships are exactly the fixed resident slots' image defaults — no more, no fewer. | [`architecture/persona-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/persona-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-PERS-006` | an installed persona that any readable-or-restorable binding tuple still names is never removed — single removal and the sweep both refuse it, and a reference set that cannot be computed refuses too. | [`architecture/persona-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/persona-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-PERS-007` | Applying a persona to a resident stages the binding rather than activating it, and a candidate that fails the compile proof leaves the binding store untouched. | [`architecture/persona-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/persona-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-PERS-009` | Every section body a persona's Markdown declares reaches the text projection exactly once. | [`architecture/personality.md`](../architecture/personality.md) |
| `INV-PERS-010` | A committing persona reconciliation that refuses logs exactly one structured record stating, for each of the active and staged selections, whether it was absent (no directory entry), unreadable — naming its file and failure class — or read — naming its file, mode and persona ref, carrying pin and config-relative restore facts for an active selection the reload dispatches through its non-image-default arm and for a staged selection only where reconciliation selects it as an override, and a found checksum only where a pack actually resolved; when the pass staged a candidate before failing, the staged observation reflects that candidate; and the structured record names no recovery requiring the live runtime. | [`architecture/personality.md`](../architecture/personality.md) |
| `INV-PERS-011` | A persona install approval recorded at the tap, whose configurator run Casa could not start, does not leave the card claiming the configurator is carrying on: the approval stays recorded and approved, the card says the run could not be started and that the approval is kept, and the one edit is chosen from the launch's report rather than written before it. | [`architecture/persona-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/persona-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-PERS-012` | A persona-bound resident's `prompts/system.md` is read only into the composed fallback prompt and is not served when its compiled bundle is active; and an agent's write to a resident's copy through `Write`, `Edit`, `MultiEdit` or `NotebookEdit` is refused on the executor, resident and delegated-resident hook paths. | [`architecture/prompt-file-guards.md`](../architecture/prompt-file-guards.md) |
| `INV-PERS-013` | A persona ref that arrives through a persona tool — a swap, a reset, an apply, an install commit, a removal or the sweep — has its id and version segments validated against the shared canonical patterns before any path join under the approved roots, and where the tool loads a pack to bind it — a swap, a reset, an apply — the pack must declare the identity the ref names; so a traversal-bearing ref never reaches a caller-facing persona path join and a mis-parked pack is never bound under a ref it does not declare. | [`architecture/persona-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/persona-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-PERS-015` | A rule stated in the shipped safety kernel is present in every resident projection on every surface. | [`architecture/personality.md`](../architecture/personality.md) |
| `INV-PERS-016` | An installed specialist whose active binding's role checksum differs from the role the loader materialized — with the component root, persona identity triple, configuration and dependency closure unchanged — is activated on a binding re-derived for that role; on a committing load of an enabled specialist the re-derived binding replaces the active tuple in place, leaving the retained prior and any staged candidate untouched, while a validation-only load and a disabled specialist write nothing; and a binding whose persona identity or agent id differs from what the loader resolved is refused, never re-derived. | [`architecture/personality.md`](../architecture/personality.md) |
| `INV-PERS-017` | A persona-bound resident's per-agent `response_shape.yaml` is read and rendered into the composed fallback prompt, and no part of it is served while its compiled bundle is active; and an agent's write to a resident's copy through `Write`, `Edit`, `MultiEdit` or `NotebookEdit` is refused on the executor, resident and delegated-resident hook paths. | [`architecture/prompt-file-guards.md`](../architecture/prompt-file-guards.md) |
| `INV-PERS-018` | Every entry point that stages a persona binding for a resident tells the operator what the promoting restart costs — the same notice in its result envelope and in its own description — and the apply recipe states it at the step that orders the restart. | [`architecture/persona-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/persona-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-PERS-019` | Each shipped resident role admits, at `persona_apply`, its own slot's persona and any `demo/` pack in the version range `>=0.1.0 <1.0.0`, and refuses another namespace, a version outside that range and a sibling resident's persona, writing nothing. | [`architecture/persona-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/persona-lifecycle.md) |
| `INV-PERS-020` | The ref literal `latest`, given to a persona inspection, resolves before anything is staged to the tag INV-PLUG-022 chooses; the result reports that tag as `resolved_ref`, never the literal, the fetch is guarded against its peel, and a repository with no published release is refused with `no_release_found`, staging nothing. | [`architecture/persona-lifecycle.md`](../architecture/persona-lifecycle.md) |
